interactive_prompts.name: trust_prompt_no_default
interactive_prompts.regex: (?s)❯ No, exit.{0,80}Yes, I trust this folder.{0,120}Enter to confirm · Esc to cancel\s*\z
interactive_prompts.note: claude v2.1.252 folder-trust dialog (live-captured 2026-09-01): options UNNUMBERED, default flipped to '❯ No, exit' — the v2.1.193 rule's Enter would confirm No and kill the REPL (this burned all three wave-20260901b lanes). Down,Enter verified live: Down moves ❯ to 'Yes, I trust this folder', Enter boots a trusted REPL. BOTTOM-ANCHORED (footer + \z + tail_lines 12 + distance bounds, plan_approval discipline) so tracked files quoting the dialog cannot self-match when rendered. Disjoint by construction from trust_prompt (requires ❯ No, exit; that one requires the numbered ❯ 1. Yes line). Version-tolerant: a future Yes-default build stops matching and falls through. once:true. Source: docs/incidents/2026-09-01-claude-2252-trust-default-flip.md

interactive_prompts.name: trust_prompt
interactive_prompts.regex: (?s)❯ 1\.\s+Yes, I trust this folder.{0,120}Enter to confirm.{0,40}\s*\z
interactive_prompts.note: claude v2.1.193 folder-trust dialog (numbered options, Yes pre-highlighted): one Enter confirms Yes, verified live 2026-06-26. Kept for older builds; v2.1.252's unnumbered No-default dialog is trust_prompt_no_default above — the two regexes are DISJOINT BY CONSTRUCTION (this one requires the numbered ❯ 1. Yes line; that one requires ❯ No, exit), so array order is irrelevant for correctness. BOTTOM-ANCHORED on the Enter-to-confirm footer + tail_lines per the plan_approval discipline (2026-09-02: the unanchored form self-matched this repo's own tracked files when rendered by an agent — see the self-match guard test). The ❯ cursor collides with the REPL marker, so tickDuringBoot dismisses it before prompt delivery. once:true — lingering-scrollback discipline. Source: docs/incidents/2026-09-01-claude-2252-trust-default-flip.md

interactive_prompts.name: askuserquestion_multiselect
interactive_prompts.note: claude AskUserQuestion multiSelect: '[ ]' checkboxes + the 'Enter to select' menu footer. Verified 2026-05-26: Enter toggles the highlighted checkbox, Right moves to the Submit tab, Enter submits → recommended_or_first (keystrokes are PACED — see autoRespondInterKeyPause). Requires BOTH a '[ ]' checkbox AND the menu footer so a bare markdown checklist in agent output ('1. [ ] do thing') does NOT false-match, and so the rule keeps matching after the first checkbox toggles (other rows stay '[ ]') — enabling a retry if the first submit misses. MUST precede askuserquestion_select: a multi-select pane also contains that footer, so the checkbox rule must win (first-match). --dangerously-skip-permissions does NOT suppress this (a question is not a permission).

interactive_prompts.name: askuserquestion_select
interactive_prompts.note: claude AskUserQuestion single-select: first option pre-highlighted ('❯ 1.'); footer 'Enter to select · ↑/↓ to navigate · Esc to cancel'. Verified 2026-05-26: a single Enter selects the highlighted first option = recommended_or_first. Layer-2 net behind the prompt-prefix interactive policy (Layer 1).

interactive_prompts.name: plan_approval
interactive_prompts.regex: (?s)ready to execute\. Would you like to proceed\?.{0,400}2\.\s+Yes, manually approve edits.{0,300}ctrl\+g to edit in Vim.{0,200}\.md\s*\z
interactive_prompts.note: ExitPlanMode approval. Enter accepts the pre-highlighted option 1, an approval in both observed launch-mode variants. BOTTOM-ANCHORED (\z): a live dialog is always at the END of the capture, so scrollback that has scrolled up - including this repo's OWN docs and test fixtures, which quote the dialog verbatim on tracked files an agent may cat - cannot match. That single anchor closes the self-match, the answered-dialog re-fire, and the diff-line-deletion attacks together; distance bounds alone did not (a matcher that DELETES lines can shrink any gap). Tail bound 400 (live: 155, and the footer carries a variable-length plan path). Response is a bare Enter, NOT the explicit '1,Enter' the per_edit_approval note argues for: Enter is what was verified live against this dialog and '1' as a hotkey was not, and shipping an unverified keystroke is the exact class of error this rule exists to prevent. Source: docs/incidents/2026-08-27-plan-mode-dialog-blind-spot.md.

_notes_on_removed_patterns.fact_forcing_gate: REMOVED v12.1.5 after live-smoke forensics (workspace bridge-t7-G3mPzn). The ECC gateguard PreToolUse hook fires once per Write attempt and Claude recovers natively — it presents the 4 requested facts and retries the Write. Neither extend_timeout nor auto_respond is appropriate: extend_timeout doesn't help (Claude isn't slow, it's just sequencing tool calls), and auto_respond stacks identical messages at the prompt every poll-tick because the gate error remains visible in pane scrollback, interfering with Claude's own recovery. The correct bridge behavior is no rule — let Claude handle the hook natively. Re-introduce only with dedupe logic that suppresses re-fires within a single agent turn (v12.1.6+ design).
